q: Which place is the only lint check you can rely on to always run?
why: The editor needs setup and a hook can be skipped with --no-verify; CI runs on every push.
That keeps the hook fast; run pre-commit run --all-files once when you add a hook.

o: Silent changes hide what changed; a reported fix becomes a visible commit
why: In CI, just report so the fix is a commit someone reviews.

q: What makes a CI lint job fail and block a merge?
o: The linter exiting with a failure code
why: The gate works through the exit code; by default only errors cause a failure.

q: Which does NOT help keep linting fast?
why: Changed files, caches, fast tools and excludes all cut the time.

q: Editor, hook and CI should each use their own rule settings.
why: Myth: all three should read the same config file, or people get CI failures they never saw locally.
